(p-486) Sūrat al-Nūr is Madanī (Medinan), and it has sixty-four verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿A surah﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., "This is a surah." ﴿Which We have sent down﴾ is its attribute. Ṭalḥa read "sūratan" (surah) in the accusative, either as in "Zaydan ḍarabtuhu" (Zayd, I struck him), or as in "try (recite) a surah" (ut'lu sūratan). The sūrah (chapter) is a collection of sentences of verses with an opening and a closing for it; its etymology is from sūr al-madīnah (the wall of the city).

﴿And We have made obligatory﴾, i.e., its rulings contained within it. The root meaning of farḍ (obligation) is "cutting," i.e., We made it something decided upon. With the doubled letter (faṣṣalnā/farraḍnā), it is read by Makkī and Abū ʿAmr, for emphasis on the obligation and its affirmation, or because it contains various obligations, or because of the large number of those on whom it was obligated from the predecessors and those after them.

﴿And We have sent down in it clear verses﴾, i.e., clear proofs, ﴿so that you may remember﴾, i.e., that you may take heed. With the lightening of the dhāl (tadhakkarūn → taḏakkarūn), it is read by Ḥamzah, ʿAlī, Khalaf and Ḥafṣ. Then He detailed its rulings, saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 2:

﴿The fornicatress and the fornicator﴾ Its case-ending (raf') is due to it being the subject of a nominal sentence (ibtida'), and the predicate (khabar) is omitted, i.e., "what has been made obligatory upon you is: the fornicatress and the fornicator," meaning their flogging; or the predicate is "flog them." The fa' (fa'-particle) enters because the alif and lam (of al-ladhi/al-lati) carry the meaning of "the one who" (alladhi), and it is given the meaning of a conditional (shart), and its estimated form is: "the woman who commits fornication and the man who commits fornication, so flog them both," just as you say, "whoever commits fornication, flog him." It is similar to His words: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses, flog them﴾ [al-Nur: 4]. 'Isa ibn 'Umar read it in the accusative (nasb), by supposing a verb which the apparent (noun) explains, and this is better than "a surah which We have sent down," because of the imperative: ﴿So flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾. Jald (flogging) is striking the skin (jild), and in it there is an indication (p-487) that one should not exaggerate so that the pain reaches the flesh. The address is to the rulers (a'imma), because establishing the hadd (prescribed punishment) is a part of religion and it is incumbent on all, but they cannot all gather, so the imam (leader) stands in their place. This is the ruling for a free person who is not muhsan (married and chaste under the legal conditions), since the ruling for the muhsan is stoning (rajm). The conditions of ihsan that require stoning are: freedom, sanity, puberty, Islam, being married by a valid marriage contract, and consummation. This is evidence that exile (taghrib) is not prescribed, because the fa' enters only upon the jaza' (consequent), and jaza' is a noun meaning "sufficient," and the exile reported is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse, just as the confinement and harm in His words ﴿Then confine them in the houses﴾ [al-Nisa': 15] and His words ﴿Then harm them both﴾ [al-Nisa': 16] were abrogated by this verse. ﴿And let not pity (ra'fa) for them both take hold of you﴾, i.e., mercy; the vowelled fath is a dialectal form and it is the reading of Makki. It is said that ra'fa is in averting what is disliked, and rahma is in bringing about what is loved. The meaning is: it is obligatory upon the believers to be firm in the religion of Allah and not let softness take hold of them in carrying out His limits, so that they do not suspend the hudud or lighten the blows. ﴿In the religion of Allah﴾, i.e., in obedience to Allah or His judgment. ﴿If you believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ is by way of stirring up and kindling anger for the sake of Allah and His religion, and the answer of the condition is implied, i.e., "so flog, and do not suspend the hadd." ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, i.e., let them be present at the place of their hadd. Calling it "punishment" is evidence that it is a penalty. ﴿A group (ta'ifa)﴾ is a company that can be a circle, so that they may take warning and he may be deterred; the least of it is three or four, and it is a common attribute, as if it were the group surrounding something. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that it is four to forty men. ﴿Of the believers﴾, i.e., of those who affirm belief in Allah.

The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist. That is, the wicked person whose nature is adultery does not desire to marry the virtuous women; he desires only a wicked woman of his own kind, or a polytheist. And the wicked woman who fornicates is likewise: the righteous men do not desire to marry her, and only one of his own kind among the debauched or the polytheists desires her. So the verse is a discouragement from marrying prostitutes, since adultery is equivalent to polytheism in ugliness, while faith is the companion of chastity and self-restraint. This is similar to His saying: ﴿The wicked women are for wicked men, and the wicked men are for wicked women﴾ [al-Nur: 26].

It has been said that marrying an adulteress was forbidden at the beginning of Islam, and then it was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: ﴿And marry off the single among you﴾ [al-Nur: 32]. It has also been said that the intended meaning of "nikah" (marriage) here is "wati'" (sexual intercourse), because a man who is not an adulterer finds the adulteress repulsive and does not desire her. This is correct, but it leads to your saying: "The adulterer does not commit adultery except with an adulteress, and the adulteress is not committed with except by an adulterer."

The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about one who committed adultery with a woman and then married her, and he said: "Its beginning is fornication and its end is marriage."

The meaning of the first clause is a description of the adulterer as one who does not desire chaste women but desires the immoral ones. The meaning of the second clause is a description of the adulteress as one who is not desired by the chaste but only by fornicators. These are two different meanings. The adulteress was placed before the adulterer first, and then the adulterer was placed before her second. This is because the verse was brought for the punishment of both of them for what they committed, and the woman is the material from which that crime arose. If she did not tempt the man, did not signal to him, and did not allow him access, he would not have desired or succeeded. Since she is the root of this, she is mentioned first. As for the second clause, it is directed toward mentioning marriage, and the man is the root in that, since he is the one who proposes and the beginning of the request comes from him.

It was recited as "lā yankiḥ" (with the jussive), as a prohibition (nahy). The indicative (marfu') reading also carries the sense of prohibition, but it is more emphatic and forceful. It may also be a pure report, meaning that their custom runs in this manner. Yet it is incumbent upon the believer not to put himself under this custom, and to guard himself against it. ﴿And that has been forbidden to the believers﴾, that is, adultery or marrying prostitutes for the purpose of earning money through adultery, or because of what it contains of resembling the sinners, presence at places of suspicion, causing evil talk about oneself, backbiting, and sitting with the sinners. How much of this exposes one to committing sins? So how about being joined in marriage to whores and harlots?!

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 4:

﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾. With a kasra on the ṣād (*muḥṣanāt* read as *muḥṣināt*), ʿAlī read it. That is, they accuse free, chaste, Muslim women who are legally responsible of zina (fornication). Qadhf (slander, false accusation) can be by zina or by other things, but what is meant here is accusing them of zina, by saying "O adulteress." This is indicated by the mention of the chaste women right after the adulteresses (*zawānī*), and by the requirement of four witnesses in His words ﴿then they do not bring four witnesses﴾, that is, then they do not bring four witnesses who testify to zina. This is because qadhf with something other than zina, such as saying "O sinner, O eater of usury," requires only two witnesses, and the offender is subject to ta'zir (discretionary punishment). The conditions for being muḥṣan in qadhf are freedom, sanity, puberty, Islam, and chastity from zina. The muḥṣan male is like the muḥṣana female in the obligation of the hadd (the prescribed punishment) for qadhf. ﴿Flog them eighty lashes﴾, if the accuser is free. *Thamānīna* (eighty) is in the accusative as a verbal noun, just as *mi'ata jaldah* (a hundred lashes) is, and *jaldatan* (lashes) is in the accusative of specification (tamyīz). ﴿And never accept their testimony﴾. The word *shahāda* (testimony) is indefinite in a negative context, so it covers every testimony. According to us, the rejection of testimony is part of the hadd and is tied to carrying out the hadd or part of it, as is known. According to al-Shafiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, the rejection of their testimony is tied to the qadhf itself. So according to us, the consequent of the condition, which is the accusation, is the flogging, and the rejection of testimony is permanent, that is, for the duration of their lives. ﴿And those are the defiant ones﴾. This is a resumed sentence, not part of the consequent of the condition, as if it describes the state of the accusers before Allah after the conditional clause has ended.

Al-Nasafi, Madarik al-Tanzil, on Surah 24, verse 5:

And His saying ﴿except those who repent after that﴾, i.e., after the slander (qadhf), ﴿and amend﴾ their conditions. It is an exception (istithna') from ﴿the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Nur: 4]. It is indicated by ﴿then surely Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾, i.e., He forgives their sins and has mercy upon them. The exception, according to us (the Hanafi school), should be in the accusative (mansub), because it is an exception from an affirmed statement (mujab; i.e., a positive, non-negated clause). But according to the one who made the exception connected to the second sentence, it should be in the genitive (majrur) as a substitute (badal) for the pronoun "hum" in "lahum".

Having mentioned the ruling on slandering chaste women who are not one's wives, he [God] then explained the ruling on slandering wives, saying: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾, i.e., who charge their wives with adultery, ﴿and have no witnesses except themselves﴾, i.e., they have no one to testify for them to confirm their claim. ﴿Except themselves﴾ is in the nominative as a substitute (badal) for "witnesses" (shuhada').

﴿Then the testimony of each of them is four﴾ — with the nominative (raf') read by the Kufans other than Abu Bakr, taking it as the predicate (khabar) of the subject "fa-shahadatu ahadihim." On this reading, its predicate is omitted, and its estimated form is: "fa-wajibun shahadatu ahadihim arba'" (so the testimony of each of them being four is obligatory). ﴿Testimonies by God; indeed he is surely among the truthful﴾, regarding what he has charged her with of adultery.

﴿And the fifth﴾: There is a difference of opinion regarding the grammatical case (raf', nominative) of الخامِسَةُ (al-khamisah, "the fifth") here. According to the well-known view, the implied phrase is "and the fifth testimony [is]" ﴿that the curse of Allah be upon him﴾. So it is a subject (mubtada') and predicate (khabar) ﴿if he is among the liars﴾ concerning what he accused her of, namely adultery.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 8:

﴿And it averts from her the punishment﴾ — it repels from her the confinement (al-habs). The subject of yadra'u (it averts) is ﴿that she testifies four testimonies by God that he [the husband] is indeed among the liars﴾ — that is, the husband is among the liars regarding what he accused her of, namely adultery (al-zina).

﴿And the fifth [testimony]: that the wrath of God be upon her if he is among the truthful﴾, i.e., the husband, regarding what he has accused her of, namely adultery. Hafs read *al-khamisata* in the accusative, as a conjunction with ﴿four testimonies﴾ [al-Nur: 8], while others read it in the nominative, as the beginning of a sentence, with *anna ghadaba Allahi* as its predicate. Nafi' read *anna la'nata Allahi* and *anna ghadiba Allahi* with a light (*mukhaffafa*) *anna* and a kasra on the *dad*, and they carry the same grammatical force as the heavy (*mushaddada*) form. *Anna ghadaba Allahi* with a light *anna* is read by Sahl, Ya'qub and Hafs. The wrath is attributed to her side, because women use cursing (*al-la'n*) frequently, as the hadith reports. Thus they may become bold in committing [the offence], through the frequency with which cursing passes over their tongues and its weight leaves their hearts. So the wrath is mentioned on their side, so that it may act as a deterrent for them.

The principle is this: according to us, *li'an* (mutual oath-imprecation, the sworn mutual testimony accompanied by curses) consists of testimonies strengthened by oaths and joined with cursing. It takes the place of the punishment for slander (*hadd al-qadhf*) with regard to the husband, and the punishment for adultery (*hadd al-zina*) with regard to the wife, because God Most High named it a testimony. So when a husband accuses his wife of adultery, and both of them are among those competent to testify, the *li'an* between them is valid. When they have performed *li'an*, as explained in *al-Nahr*, separation does not occur until the judge separates them. According to Zufar, may God have mercy on him, separation occurs by their mutual cursing, and the separation is an irrevocable single divorce (*taliqa ba'ina*). According to Abu Yusuf, Zufar and al-Shafi'i, it is a permanent prohibition of marriage (*tahrim mu'abbad*).

"The verse of *li'an* was revealed concerning Hilal ibn Umayya or 'Uwaymir, when he said: 'I found Shurayk ibn Sahma upon the belly of my wife Khawla,' and she denied it, so the Prophet (ﷺ) made them perform *li'an* between them."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 10:

﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah﴾ — His favour (tafaddul) — ﴿upon you, and His mercy﴾ — His blessing (ni'mah) — ﴿and that Allah is Tawwab (Oft-Returning, Accepting of repentance), Hakim (All-Wise)﴾. The answer to "lawla" (were it not for) is omitted, meaning: "He would have exposed you" (la-fada-hakum), or "He would have hastened punishment upon you" (la-'ajalakum bil-'uqubah).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 11:

﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander﴾ (al-ifk) is the most intense form of lying and fabrication. Its root is al-afk, which means "turning," because it is a statement turned away from its true face. The intended meaning is the slander that was fabricated against ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her. ʿĀʾisha said: "I lost a necklace during the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq, so I fell behind. Nobody noticed that the howdah was empty, because of my lightness. When they set off, Safwan ibn al-Muʿattal made his camel kneel for me, and he led it until he reached them after they had halted. Whoever was destined to perish among us perished. I fell ill for a month, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to ask, 'How are you?' and I did not see any gentleness from him that I was used to seeing. Then the aunt of my father, Umm Mistah, stumbled, and she said, 'Misṭaḥ has come to ruin.' I rebuked her for this, and she informed me of the slander. When I heard it, my illness increased. I spent the night at my parents' house; my tears did not stop, and I could not sleep, and they both thought that the weeping would split my liver. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Rejoice, O Ḥumayrāʾ, for Allah has revealed your innocence.' I said: 'By the praise of Allah, not by your praise.'"

﴿A band﴾ (ʿuṣba) is a group of ten to forty people; it means they gathered together (iʿṣaʿṣabū). They were ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy, the head of the hypocrites; Zayd ibn Rifaʿa; Ḥassān ibn Thābit; Misṭaḥ ibn Uthātha; Ḥimna bint Jaḥsh; and those who supported them. ﴿From among you﴾ means from the community of the Muslims. They thought that the slander had come only from the disbelievers, not from those among the believers.

﴿Do not think it﴾, that is, the slander, ﴿to be evil for you﴾ in the sight of Allah. ﴿Rather, it is good for you﴾, because Allah rewarded you for it, and He revealed eighteen verses concerning the clearing of ʿĀʾisha from it. The address is to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, ʿĀʾisha, Safwan, and whoever among the believers was distressed by that.

﴿For every person among them is what he earned of sin﴾, meaning: for every person of the band is a recompense for his sin according to the degree of his involvement in it. Some of them laughed, some spoke about it, and some remained silent.

﴿And the one who took upon himself its greatest part﴾, that is, its magnitude, (p-492) ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy, ﴿among them﴾, that is, among the band, ﴿for him is a great punishment﴾, that is, Jahannam. It is related that Safwan passed by her howdah while he was among a company of his people. He said, "Who is this?" They said, "ʿĀʾisha." He said, "By Allah, she has not escaped from it, nor has it escaped from her." Then he rebuked those who were engaged in the slander, and he said...

﴿Why did you not﴾ say, when you heard it, that is, the slander, ﴿the believing men and believing women think well of their own kind﴾ concerning those among them. The believers are like a single soul, as in His saying: ﴿And do not defame one another﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11]. ﴿Good﴾ means chastity and righteousness. This is like what is related: "Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), 'I am certain of the lie of the hypocrites, because Allah protected you from a fly landing on your skin, since it lands on filth and gets smeared with it. When Allah protected you from that small amount of filth, how could He not protect you from keeping company with one who is smeared with such an abomination?'" Uthman said, "Allah did not cast your shadow upon the earth so that no person would place his foot upon that shadow. Since He did not permit anyone to place a foot on your shadow, how could He permit anyone to defile the honour of your wife?" Likewise Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Jibril informed you that there was filth on your sandals and commanded you to remove the sandal from your foot because of the filth that clung to it. How then would he not command you to remove it, supposing you were smeared with some of the abominations?"

It is also related that Abu Ayyub al-Ansari said to his wife, "Do you not see what is being said?" She replied, "If you were in Safwan's place, would you think ill of the sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said, "No." She said, "If I were in Aisha's place, I would not have betrayed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Aisha is better than me, and Safwan is better than you."

He turned from direct address (*khitab*) to third-person address (*ghaybah*), and from the pronoun to the explicit noun. ﴿And they said, "This is a manifest lie."﴾ [Cf. al-Nur: 13, ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾]

He did not say "you thought well of your own kind," but "you said," in order to intensify the rebuke through a shift of person (*iltifat*). Moreover, the explicit use of the word "believers" indicates that the sharing of faith requires that no believing man should credit against his brother, nor any believing woman against her sister, the words of one who finds fault or slanders. This is part of the good manners whose practitioners and guardians are few. Would that you could find one who, on hearing such a thing, keeps silent and does not spread what he heard among his brethren. ﴿And they said, "This is a manifest lie."﴾ That is, an obvious falsehood that is not fitting for either of them.

(p-493)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 13:

﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾ Why did they not bring, for the slander, if they were truthful, four witnesses? ﴿Then since they did not bring the witnesses,﴾ the four ones, ﴿then those, in the sight of Allah,﴾ meaning: in His judgment and His law, ﴿they are the liars,﴾ meaning the slanderers. This is because Allah, exalted is He, made the distinction between the truthful and the false accusation to be the establishment or the absence of the testimony of the four witnesses. And those who accused ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, had no evidence for their claim, so they were liars.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 14:

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into.﴾ "Lawla" (lit. "were it not for") here indicates the non-existence of one thing due to the existence of another, unlike what came before. That is: "And were it not that I decreed to bestow favour upon you in this world with various kinds of blessings, among which is granting you respite for repentance, and to show you mercy in the Hereafter through pardon and forgiveness, I would have hastened punishment upon you for what you plunged into of the discourse of slander." It is said: afada fi al-hadith (he launched into the talk), khada (he plunged in), and indafa'a (he rushed into it).

**﴿When﴾** is an adverb of time (*zarf*) governed either by **﴿touched you﴾** or by **﴿you would have been overwhelmed﴾**. **﴿You were receiving it﴾**: some of you were taking it from one another. It is said: تَلَقّى القَوْلَ (*talaqqā al-qawl*), وتَلَقَّنَهُ (*talaqqanahu*), and وتَلَقَّفَهُ (*talaqqafahu*), all meaning he received the speech. **﴿With your tongues﴾**: that is, some of you would say to others, "Has the report about 'Ā'ishah reached you?" until it spread among them and circulated, so that no house or gathering remained without it having flown through it. **﴿And you say with your mouths what you have no knowledge of﴾**: the phrase is qualified by "mouths" although speech only comes from the mouth, because a known matter has its knowledge in the heart, and then the tongue expresses it. This slander was only a saying that circulated on your lips without being an expression of knowledge held in the heart. This is like His saying: **﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾** (Āl ʿImrān 3:167). **﴿And you reckon it﴾**, that is, your engaging in speculation about ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, **﴿insignificant﴾**, a minor matter, **﴿while it is, with Allah, grave﴾**, a major sin. Some people, when dying, were distressed, and when asked about this they said, "I fear a sin that never occurred to my mind," yet it is, with Allah, grave. (p. 494)

ۚ﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say: "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander"﴾ (The Arabic word هَلّا means "why not" or "would that"). The adverbial phrase (إذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ, "when you heard it") is placed between لَوْلا and قُلْتُمْ, because adverbs of time have a special status: they are treated as if they were the things themselves, since events occur within them and they are inseparable from those events. For this reason, latitude is permitted with them that is not permitted with other parts of speech. The purpose of placing the adverb first is that it was obligatory upon them, as soon as they heard the slander, to refrain from speaking it. Since mention of the time was more important, it was placed first. The meaning is: ﴿Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander.﴾ ﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it again, if you are believers﴾ [al-Nur: 17].

Why did you not say, when you heard the slander, that it is not right for us to speak of this? ﴿Glory be to You!﴾ is an expression of wonder at the magnitude of the matter. The sense of wonder in the word "tasbih" (glorification) is that, originally, God is glorified upon seeing something wondrous in His creation, and then its usage broadened until it was applied to anything that is marvelled at. Alternatively, it expresses God's exaltation above the possibility that the sanctity of His Prophet be defiled. The reason it is permissible for the wife of a Prophet to be an unbeliever, like the wives of Noah and Lot, but not to be unchaste, is that the Prophet is sent to the unbelievers in order to call them, so there must be nothing with him that would repel them from him. Unbelief does not repel them, but lewdness (al-kashkhana) is among the greatest of repellents. ﴿This is a tremendous slander﴾: a falsehood that stupefies whoever hears it. ﴿Tremendous﴾. It was mentioned earlier as "a manifest falsehood" (ifk mubin). It is also possible that they were commanded to say both, as an exaggeration in disavowal.

Allah admonishes you that you should never return to the like of this (slander, or listening to such talk), as long as you are alive and accountable, if you are believers. The phrase "if you are believers" serves to stir them up so that they take heed, and it reminds them of what necessitates abandoning such a return, namely faith, which restrains from every ugly deed.

{And Allah makes the signs clear for you} — the clear proofs, the rulings of the laws, and the beautiful etiquettes. {And Allah is All-Knowing} of you and of your deeds, {All-Wise} — He recompenses in accordance with your deeds. Or: He knew the truth of her purity and judged her innocence.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 19:

﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe﴾ i.e., that which is extremely ugly. The meaning is: they spread indecency deliberately, with the intention of spreading it and out of love for it. ﴿For them is a painful punishment in this world﴾ by the prescribed punishment (al-hadd), and indeed the Prophet (ﷺ) gave Ibn Ubayy, Hassan and Mistah the prescribed punishment. ﴿And the Hereafter﴾ by the Fire, which He promised if they do not repent. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ the hidden matters and the secrets of hearts, ﴿but you do not know﴾. i.e., He knows the love of whoever loves the spreading of indecency, and He will punish him for it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 20:

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you, and His mercy﴾ [He would have hastened the punishment for you]. He repeated the favour by withholding the hastening of punishment, and the answer (jawab) is omitted for the sake of emphasis regarding the favour upon them and the rebuke directed at them. ﴿And that Allah is Most Kind (ra'uf)﴾ in that He manifested the innocence of the one slandered and granted reward, ﴿Most Merciful (rahim)﴾ in forgiving the offence of the slanderer if he repents.

O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. (That is: his traces and his whisperings, by listening to the slander and speaking about it.) And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan - indeed, he (i.e., Satan) commands immorality (fahsha', that whose ugliness is extreme) and wrongdoing (munkar, that which souls find objectionable, so they recoil from it and do not approve of it). And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been purified (zakā). (Were it not that Allah graciously granted you repentance that expiates sins, none of you would ever have been cleansed of the filth of the sin of slander, for all time.) But Allah purifies whom He wills - He accepts the repentance of the penitent when they make it sincere. And Allah is Hearing of what they say, Knowing of their inner states and their sincerity.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 22:

﴿And let not those of virtue and affluence among you swear off﴾ (wa-la ya'tali): meaning, let them not swear; it is from ii'talā, which means to swear, a form of iftiʿāl derived from al-ulyah (oath), or: let them not fall short, from al-alw (falling short). ﴿those of virtue (ūlū al-faḍl) among you﴾ in religion ﴿and affluence﴾ in worldly life ﴿to give﴾ ﴿to the near of kin, the needy, and those who emigrated in the way of Allah﴾, that is: let them not swear that they will not do good to those deserving of kindness, or let them not restrict themselves in doing good to them, even if there is enmity between them because of an offence they committed. ﴿And let them pardon and overlook﴾. Al-ʿafw is covering (over), and al-ṣafḥ is turning away; that is: let them overlook the harshness and turn away from punishment. ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?﴾ So let them do to them what they hope Allah, their Lord, will do to them despite the abundance of their sins. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾. So adopt the manners of Allah: forgive and show mercy.

It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, when he swore that he would not spend on Mistah ibn Uthatha, his maternal cousin, because of his involvement in the matter of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her. Mistah was a poor man, a veteran of Badr and an emigrant. When the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it to Abu Bakr, he said: "Yes, I love that Allah forgive me," and he restored his maintenance to Mistah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 23:

﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste women﴾ (al-muhsanat), the modest ones, ﴿who are unaware﴾ (al-ghafilat), the ones whose hearts are sound and pure, in whom there is no cunning or deceit, because they have not experienced such affairs, ﴿who are believers﴾ (al-mu'minat), in what must be believed in.

From Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: they are the wives of the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace. It was also said: they are all believing women, since the lesson lies in the generality of the wording and not in the specific occasion of revelation (al-'ibrah bi-'umum al-lafz la bi-khusus al-sabab). It was also said: 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, alone is meant, and the plural was used because whoever slanders one of the wives of the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, is as if he slanders all of them.

﴿They are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and theirs is a great punishment﴾. He made the slanderers cursed in both abodes, and threatened them with a great punishment in the Hereafter if they do not repent.

The governing element (al-'amil) of "on the day their tongues, hands and feet will testify against them" (yawma tashhadu 'alayhim) is "they will be punished" (yu'adhdhabun). Hamzah and 'Ali read it with the ya' (wa-bil-ya' Hamzah wa-'Ali), i.e., "yashhadu" with the ya'.

"Their tongues and their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do." That is, concerning what they fabricated (afakū) or slandered (bahatū).

The governing word for ﴿on that day Allah will pay them their due recompense in full﴾, in the accusative (بِالنَصْبِ), is a qualifier (صِفَةٌ) of "dīnahum" (their due). The dīn here is the recompense (الجَزاءُ). The meaning of "al-ḥaqq" (the true) is "the established, that which they truly deserve" (الثابِتُ الَّذِي هم أهْلُهُ).

Mujāhid read it in the nominative (بِالرَفْعِ) as a qualifier, like the reading of Ubayy: "Allah will pay them, the Truth, their due recompense" (يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللهُ الحَقُّ دِينَهُمْ). On the accusative reading, "al-ḥaqq" may also be a qualifier of Allah, in the accusative by way of praise (عَلى المَدْحِ): ﴿and they will know﴾ at that time ﴿that Allah is the Manifest Truth﴾ (al-ḥaqq al-mubīn), (p-497) because doubts will be removed and necessary knowledge (العِلْمِ الضَرُورِيِّ) will be attained.

Allah the Exalted did not stress any of the sins in the Qur'an as He stressed the slander (إفْكِ) against ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her. He was concise about it and yet expansive, detailed and yet summary, emphatic and yet repetitive. There is no reason for this except a matter of importance.

It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him: "Whoever commits a sin and then repents from it, his repentance is accepted, except whoever engages in the matter of ʿĀʾishah." This is from him an exaltation and an emphasis on the gravity of the slander.

Allah the Exalted cleared four (persons): He cleared Yūsuf (ʿalayhi al-salām) by a witness from her own family; Mūsā (ʿalayhi al-salām) from the claim of the Jews about him, by the stone that took away his garment; Maryam (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhā) by making her child speak; and ʿĀʾishah (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhā) by these great verses in His inimitable Book recited upon the face of time, with these emphases. So consider how far apart these are from the exoneration of those others. This was only to manifest the exalted rank of His Messenger and to draw attention to the lofty station of his position (ﷺ) and of his family.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 24, verse 26:

﴿The corrupt women﴾ of speech are said to be for ﴿the corrupt men﴾ and women, ﴿and the corrupt men﴾ among them ﴿are for the corrupt women﴾ of speech. Likewise, ﴿the good women are for the good men, and the good men are for the good women. Those are cleared of what they say﴾, meaning: concerning them. "﴿Those﴾" is a reference to the good people, and that they are cleared of what the corrupt say, the corrupt words, which is a statement that functions as a proverb, regarding ʿĀʾisha, may God be pleased with her, and what was attributed to her of speech that does not match her state of purity and goodness. It is also possible that it refers to the People of the House (ahl al-bayt), and that they are cleared of what the people of the slander (ahl al-ifk, the slanderers) say. It is also possible that "the corrupt women and the good women" means corrupt women who marry corrupt men, and corrupt men who marry corrupt women, and likewise the people of goodness. ﴿For them is forgiveness﴾: the phrase *mustaʾnaf* (a new, independent sentence) or *khabar baʿda khabar* (a second predicate after a predicate), ﴿and a noble provision﴾ in Paradise. Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with them both, entered upon ʿĀʾisha, may God be pleased with her, during her illness, and she was fearful of coming before God, the Exalted. He said: "Do not fear, for you will come only to forgiveness and a noble provision," and he recited the verse. She fainted from joy at what he recited. ʿĀʾisha, may God be pleased with her, said: "I have been given nine things that no other woman has been given. Gabriel came down with my image in his palm when he (ﷺ) was commanded to marry me. He married me as a virgin, and he married no other virgin besides me. He (ﷺ) died, peace and blessings be upon him, with his head in my lap, and he was buried in my house. Revelation came down to him while I was under his covering. I am the daughter of his successor (*khalifa*) and his close friend (*ṣadīq*). My innocence came down from the heavens. I was created good for a good man, and I was promised forgiveness and a noble provision."

Hassan said, defending her:

*Chaste, dignified, never accused of doubtful conduct, and she wakes up hungry for the flesh of the heedless (unsuspecting).*

*The wife of the best of people in religion and lineage, the Prophet of guidance and abundant noble deeds.*

*The noble lady of a tribe of Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib, whose noble lineage is of unfading glory.*

*Refined, whom God has perfumed her tent and purified from every blemish and falsehood.*

O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses [i.e., houses that you do not own and do not dwell in] until you have sought permission (tasta'nisu) [i.e., you ask permission] — according to Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father), who also recited it thus — and greet their occupants. Al-isti'nas (seeking familiarity, i.e., asking permission) originally means seeking information and discovering, from the verb form istif'al of anasa al-shay', meaning he saw the thing clearly and openly. That is: until you ascertain whether entry is permitted for you or not, and that is by a tasbihah (saying "Subhan Allah"), or a takbirah (saying "Allahu akbar"), or a tahmidah (saying "al-hamdu lillah"), or a clearing of the throat. And greet the occupants (wa tusallimu 'ala ahliha): the greeting (al-taslim) is that one says, "As-salamu 'alaykum, may I enter?" three times; if permission is given to him, he enters, and otherwise he returns. It has also been said that if the two meet, one initiates the greeting; otherwise, it is seeking permission. That (dhalikum), i.e., the seeking of permission and the greeting, is better for you (khayrun lakum) than the greeting of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance) and al-dumur (entering without permission). Al-dumur is entering without permission. A man of the people of the Jahiliyyah, when he entered another's house, would say, "Huyyitum sabahan, wa huyyitum masa'an" (may you be greeted in the morning, and may you be greeted in the evening), then he would enter; and it would often happen that he came upon a man with his wife under a single covering. So that you may remember (la'allakum tadhakkarun): i.e., this was said to you so that you would remember, be admonished, and act upon what you have been commanded regarding seeking permission.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 28:

﴿Then if you find no one in them﴾ in the houses, ﴿anyone [who gives permission]﴾, ﴿do not enter them until permission is given to you﴾, until you find someone who gives you permission. Or: if you find no one in them from among its people, and you have a need in them, then do not enter them except with the permission of its people, because disposing of another's property must be with his consent. ﴿And if you are told, "Go back"﴾, i.e., if there are people in it and they say, "Go back," ﴿then go back﴾, and do not insist on being admitted, nor persist in seeking to ease the screen, nor stand at the doors, because this brings about resentment. When he forbade this because it leads to resentment, it becomes obligatory to refrain from everything that leads to it, such as knocking on the door harshly, shouting at the owner of the house, and other such things. It is related from Abu 'Ubayd: "I never knocked on a scholar's door, ever." ﴿That is purer for you﴾, i.e., going back is more pleasant and purer for you, because of the safety of hearts it brings and the distance it keeps from suspicion; or it is more beneficial and increases good. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what you do﴾: a warning to those addressed that He knows what they do and what they leave undone of what they were addressed with, and so He will fully repay them for it.

"There is no sin upon you that you enter" — concerning entering: ﴿houses not inhabited﴾. He excepted from the houses for which seeking permission is required before entering, those that are not inhabited, such as caravanserais (khanat), hostels (rubut), and merchants' shops (hawanit al-tujjar). ﴿Wherein is provision for you﴾: that is, benefit, such as shelter from heat and cold, lodging for travellers and goods, and buying and selling. It was also said: the ruined dwellings (kharibat) in which one relieves oneself, and "provision" (mata') means relieving oneself. ﴿And Allah knows what you disclose and what you conceal﴾: a warning to those who enter ruined dwellings and uninhabited houses of people of suspicion (ahl al-ribah).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 30:

﴿Say to the believing men that they lower their gaze﴾ "Min" (مِن) here is partitive (lit-tab'idh), and what is meant is lowering the gaze from what is forbidden and confining it to what is permitted. ﴿and guard their private parts﴾ from fornication. The word "min" is not repeated here, because fornication has no concession (rukhsa) in any way. Looking at the face of a non-mahram woman, her hands and her feet (according to one report) is permissible, as is looking at the head of mahram relatives, the chest, the shins and the upper arms. ﴿That﴾ i.e., lowering the gaze and guarding the private parts ﴿is purer for them﴾ i.e., more cleansed from the defilement of sin. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do﴾. In this there is both encouragement and warning, meaning: He is Aware of their states and their actions, and of how they lower their eyes deceitfully. ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir: 19]. So when they recognize this, they should be mindful and cautious of Him in every movement and stillness.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 31:

﴿And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their private parts﴾. They were commanded to lower their gaze, so it is not permissible for a woman to look at a non-mahram (a man she may marry, as opposed to a mahram, a close relative she may never marry) from below his navel to his knees. If she desires, she should lower her gaze entirely. She should not look at a woman except at what is similar to that. Lowering her gaze from non-mahram men altogether is more fitting for her. The reason that lowering the gaze was mentioned before guarding the private parts is that the gaze is the messenger of adultery and the guide to immorality. The seed of desire is the eye's longing. ﴿And not to display their adornment﴾. Adornment (zina) is what a woman adorns herself with, such as jewelry, kohl, or dye. The meaning is: they should not display the places of adornment. Displaying the adornment itself, which is jewelry and the like, is permissible, so what is meant is its places, or the displaying of it while it is in its places, for the purpose of showing those places and not the items themselves. Its places are the head, the ears, the neck, the chest, the upper arms, the forearms, and the shins. Thus, the crown (iklil), the earring, the necklace, the sash, the armlet, the bracelet, the bangle, and the anklet belong to the places of adornment. ﴿Except what appears of it﴾. Except what custom and natural disposition have made apparent, which is the face, the two hands, and the two feet. Covering these would cause clear hardship, since a woman cannot avoid handling things with her hands, and there is a need to uncover her face especially in testimony, litigation, and marriage. She is also compelled to walk on the roads, with her feet exposed, especially poor women. ﴿And let them draw﴾ (wa-liyadribna), meaning let them place, from your saying "I struck my hand on the wall" when you place it upon it. ﴿Their khimar (headcover)﴾, the plural of khimar. ﴿Over their juyub (chests/necklines)﴾. The reading with the jim vowelled with a damma is that of Madani, Basri, and 'Asim. Their necklines used to be wide, so their chests and what surrounds them would show. They used to draw their headcovers behind them, leaving the front exposed, so they were commanded to draw them down in front until they cover them. ﴿Except to their husbands﴾, the plural of ba'l (husband). ﴿Or their fathers﴾, which includes grandfathers. ﴿Or the fathers of their husbands﴾, for they have become mahrams. ﴿Or their sons﴾, which includes grandsons. ﴿Or the sons of their husbands﴾, for they too have become mahrams. ﴿Or their brothers, or the sons of their brothers, or the sons of their sisters﴾, which includes grandsons and all other mahrams by implication, such as paternal and maternal uncles and others. ﴿Or their women﴾, meaning free women, because the unrestricted use of this term includes free women. ﴿Or those their right hands possess﴾, meaning their female slaves. It is not permissible for a male slave of hers to look at these places on her, whether he is a eunuch, impotent, or fully able. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: "Let the surah of al-Nur not deceive you, for it refers to female slaves and not to males." It is reported from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she permitted her male slave to look at her. ﴿Or male attendants who have no desire (ghayri)﴾. The reading with the accusative (ghayra) is that of the Syrian reader, Yazid, and Abu Bakr, as an exception or as a circumstantial qualifier. The others read it in the genitive (ghayri), as an apposition or as a qualifier. ﴿Who have no need of women﴾, meaning who have no need for women. It is said they are those who follow you to get some of your food, and have no need for women because they are simpletons who know nothing of such matters, or they are righteous elders, or impotent men, or eunuchs, or effeminate men. It is reported that it refers to one who has been castrated. The first interpretation is the most apparent. ﴿Among men﴾, a circumstantial qualifier. ﴿Or children who have not yet become aware of the nakedness of women﴾. The word "children" here is a collective noun, so it may be used in the plural sense. This means they have not come to know it due to lack of desire, from the expression "zahara 'ala al-shay'" (he became aware of the thing), meaning he came to know it. Or it means they have not reached the age of being capable of intercourse, from "zahara 'ala Fulan" (he overpowered him), meaning he became strong against him. ﴿And let them not stamp their feet so that what they conceal of their adornment becomes known﴾. Women used to strike the ground with their feet when they walked so that the jingling of their anklets would be heard, and thus it would be known that they wore anklets. They were forbidden from this, since hearing the sound of adornment is like displaying it. From this, the sound of jewelry is called waswasa (whispering). ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance together, O believers﴾. The reading "ayyuh" with a damma on the ha' is that of the Syrian reader, following the damma before it after the alif is dropped because two unvocalized letters met. The others read it with a fatha on the ha', because there is an alif after it in the underlying form. ﴿So that you may prosper﴾. The servant is never free from forgetfulness and shortcoming in carrying out Allah's commands and prohibitions, however much he strives. Therefore, He enjoined all believers to repent and gave them hope of success if they repent. It is also said: the people most in need of repentance are those who imagine they have no need to repent. The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that disobedience does not contradict faith.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 32:

﴿And marry off the unmarried among you﴾ al-ayama is the plural of ayyim (a person without a spouse), whether a man or a woman, virgin or previously married. Its original form is ayaʾim, which was transposed (qulibat). ﴿And the righteous﴾, i.e., the good (al-khayyirin) or the believers. The meaning: marry off those among you who are without spouses, of the free men and free women, and those among your ˹male and female˺ servants who are upright. ﴿of your male and female servants﴾, i.e., of your male slaves and female slaves. The command is one of recommendation (li-l-nadb), since marriage is recommended (mandub ilayhi). ﴿If they are poor﴾ in wealth, ﴿Allah will enrich them of His bounty﴾ [al-Nur: 33] through sufficiency and contentment, or through the combination of the two sustenances (rizqayn). In a hadith: "Seek provision through marriage." And it is related from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, the like of it. ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing﴾, the Rich, possessor of abundance, whose supply is not diminished by the enriching of creatures. ﴿All-Knowing﴾, He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it. It has been said that the verse is evidence that the marriage of women and the unmarried is to their guardians (awliya'), just as the marriage of slaves and female slaves is to their masters (mawali). We say: a man has no guardianship over an unmarried man except with his permission; likewise, he has no guardianship over a woman except with her permission, because the ayyim has authority over herself (yantazimuha).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 24, verse 33:

﴿And let those who cannot find a marriage keep themselves chaste﴾. Let them strive for chastity, as though the one who seeks chastity is asking Allah for chastity from himself. ﴿Who cannot find a marriage﴾ means who lacks the ability to marry, in terms of the bridal gift (*mahr*) and maintenance. ﴿Until Allah enriches them from His bounty﴾ means until He grants them the means for the bridal gift and maintenance. The Prophet ﷺ said: "O young men, whoever among you is able to bear the cost of marriage (*al-ba'ah*), let him marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the private parts. And whoever is not able, let him fast, for fasting is a shield for him." (p-503) Observe how he arranged these commands. He first commanded that which protects from temptation and keeps one away from committing disobedience, namely lowering the gaze. Then he commanded marriage, which guards the religion and suffices one against what is forbidden. Then, when one cannot marry, he commanded nobility of soul that restrains the commanding self (*nafs ammarah*) from aspiring to desire, until one becomes able to marry.

﴿And those among your slaves who seek a writing (*kitab*)﴾: that is, the slaves who ask for *kitabah* (a contract of manumission for payment, or *mukatabah*). ﴿Those who seek﴾ is in the nominative case as the subject of a new sentence, or in the accusative governed by a verb implied by what follows it, which explains it: ﴿then write for them﴾. The imperative here indicates recommendation (*nadb*). The particle *fa* (then) entered because the clause includes the sense of a condition. *Kitab* and *mukatabah* are like *'itab* and *mu'atabah* (reproach and mutual reproach). It means that a master says to his slave, "I have made a contract with you for a thousand dirhams, so if you pay it, you will be freed." Its meaning is: I write for you upon myself that you will be freed from me when you fulfil the wealth, and you write for me upon yourself that you will fulfil that; or, I write upon you the duty of paying the wealth, and I write upon myself the freeing. It is permissible for the payment to be immediate, deferred, or in installments, and also not in installments, because the command is unrestricted. ﴿If you know good in them﴾ means ability to earn, or trustworthiness and piety. The recommendation is conditional on this condition.

﴿And give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾: this is a command to the Muslims, in the sense of obligation, to assist the contract-slaves (*mukatabun*) and to give them their share of the zakat, in accordance with His words, ﴿and for the slaves﴾ [al-Tawbah: 60]. According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, its meaning is: reduce a quarter from the payment of the contract. According to us, this is by way of recommendation, and the first is the more apparent view, because *al-ita'* (giving) is transfer of ownership, so it cannot apply to a reduction.

Subayh asked his master Huwaytib to make a contract with him, but he refused, so this was revealed.

Know that slaves are of four kinds: a *qinn* (a slave kept for service), a slave authorized to trade (*ma'dhun*), a contract-slave (*mukatab*), and a runaway (*abiq*). The example of the first is the one who holds the friend of solitude, whose honour is achieved by preferring seclusion and abandoning society. The second is the friend of companionship, who is an intimate of the Presence, mixing with people for experience, looking at them with lessons, and commanding them with the good. He is the successor of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he judges by the judgment of Allah, takes for Allah, gives for Allah, understands from Allah, and speaks with Allah. The world is the marketplace of his trade, reason is the capital of his merchandise, justice in anger and in contentment is his scale, moderation in poverty and in wealth is his sign, knowledge is his refuge and his path, and the Qur'an is the book of permission from his Master. He is present among people in his outward forms and separate from them in his inner reality. He has abandoned them in what is his due from them for the sake of Allah inwardly, then connected with them in what is their due from him for the sake of Allah outwardly. (p-504) He does not live among them in the manner they live: he eats what they eat and drinks what they drink, yet who knows that he is a guest of Allah, seeing the heavens and the earth standing by His command? It is as if it was said of him:

*If the people surpass you, and you are one of them,*
*Musk is still but a part of the blood of the gazelle.*

So the state of the friend of solitude is purer and sweeter, and the state of the friend of companionship is more complete and higher. The first is placed relative to the second, in the presence of the Merciful, in the rank of the boon-companion (*nadim*) relative to the vizier before the sultan. As for the Prophet ﷺ, he is noble in both respects, the mine of both jewels, the meeting-place of both states, and the source of both sweet waters. His inner state is guided by the friend of solitude, and his outward deeds are followed by the friend of companionship.

The third is the striver, the one who takes account of himself, the worker, who is charged with the dues like the installments of a contract-slave: upon him, each day and night, are five (prayers), and in two hundred (years) five, and in a year a month (of fasting), and in a lifetime a visit (pilgrimage). It is as though he has bought himself from his Lord with these arranged installments. So he strives to free his neck, fearing to remain in the bond of servitude, and hoping to open the door of freedom, so that he may roam in the gardens of Paradise, enjoy what he wishes, and do what he desires.

The fourth is the runaways, and how many of them there are! Among them is the unjust judge, the scholar who does not act, the worker who shows off, and the preacher who does not do what he says, and most of his speech is idle, and he assaults whatever does not benefit him, not to mention the thief, the adulterer and the usurper. About such people the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah will support this religion through a people who have no portion in the Hereafter."

﴿And do not compel your young women to prostitution﴾. Ibn Ubayy had six slave-girls: Mu'adhah, Musaylah, Umaymah, Amrah, Arwa and Qatilah. He compelled them to prostitution and imposed taxes upon them. Two of them complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and this was revealed. "Young woman" (*fatah*) and "young man" (*fata*) are used as euphemisms for the female and male slave. *Bigha'* (prostitution) refers specifically to women's fornication, and it is a verbal noun of *baghat*. ﴿If they desire chastity﴾ means desire to guard themselves from fornication. He restricted the prohibition with this condition because compulsion occurs only where there is desire for chastity. The one who commands an obedient woman to prostitute herself is not called a compeller, and his command is not compulsion. Also, the verse was revealed on a particular occasion, so the prohibition fell upon that attribute. It contains a rebuke to the masters: that is, if they desire chastity, you are more entitled to it. ﴿So that you may seek the goods of the worldly life﴾: that is, so that you may seek through their compulsion to fornication their earnings and their offspring. ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: that is, to them. In the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it reads thus. Al-Hasan used to say, "By Allah, to them." Perhaps the compulsion was less than what the Shari'ah takes into account, which is compulsion that causes fear of destruction, and so she would be sinful. Or it means for them, if they repent.

And We have certainly sent down to you clear verses. With a fatha on the ya' (bi-fath al-ya'), this reading is that of the Hijazi (Meccan and Medinan) readers, the Basran reader, Abu Bakr and Hammad. The intended meaning is the verses that were made clear in this surah and explained in its rulings (ahkam) and legal limits (hudud). It is also permissible that the original form is "mubayyanan fiha" (explained within them), with the preposition dropped and the adverbial noun of place or time (zarf) used in the manner of a direct object (maf'ul bih), as in the verse "and on the day We witnessed it." With a kasra on the ya' (bi-kasriha), others read it, meaning that the verses themselves made clear the rulings and limits. The verb is then attributed to them figuratively (majaz, figurative usage), or it comes from bayyana in the sense of tabayyana (to become clear). From this comes the proverb:

Surely the dawn has made clear to one who has two eyes.

And an example from those who passed away before you: and an example from the likes of those who came before you, that is, a wondrous story from their narratives, like the story of Yusuf and Maryam, meaning the story of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her. And an admonition: what He admonished with of the verses and the examples, such as His saying, ﴿and let not compassion for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾ [al-Nur: 2], ﴿why, when you heard it﴾ [al-Nur: 12], ﴿and why, when you heard it﴾ [al-Nur: 16], ﴿Allah admonishes you never to return to the like of it﴾ [al-Nur: 17]. For the God-fearing: that is, they are the ones who benefit from them, even though it is an admonition for everyone. Compare His saying.

﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾, together with His saying ﴿the likeness of His light﴾ and ﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills﴾. It is like your saying, "Zayd is generosity and munificence," and then you say, "He uplifts people by his generosity and munificence." The meaning is: the Possessor of the light of the heavens and the earth. The Real (al-Haqq) is the one who is likened to light in its manifestness and clarity, as in His saying: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of darknesses into the light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257], that is, from falsehood to truth. He attributed the light to the heavens and the earth to indicate (p-506) the breadth of its radiance and the pervasiveness of its illumination, so that the heavens and the earth are illuminated by it. It is also permissible that what is meant is the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and that they are illuminated by it. ﴿The likeness of His light﴾, that is, the description of His light, which is wondrous in its illumination.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "﴿The likeness of His light﴾, that is, the light of Allah with which He guided the believer." Ibn Mas'ud recited, "The likeness of His light in the heart of the believer is like a niche," and Ubayy recited, "The likeness of the light of the believer."

﴿Like a niche﴾, like the description of a niche, which is a recess in a wall that is not a passage through. ﴿Therein is a lamp﴾, that is, a large, piercing lamp. ﴿The lamp is in a glass﴾, in a lantern of glass from Syria, with the zay vowelled with a kasra (zujaj). ﴿The glass is as if it were a glittering star﴾, luminous, with the dal vowelled with a damma and the ya' shadda, meaning "pearly," attributed to pearl (durr) because of the intensity of its brightness and clarity. With a kasra and a hamza, it is read by Abu Bakr and Ali, as if it repels darkness with its light. With a damma and a hamza, it is read by Abu Bakr and Hamza, and it is likened in its brightness to one of the luminous planets, such as Jupiter, Venus and the like.

﴿Is kindled﴾ with the taškhīf (lightened pronunciation) is read by Hamza, Ali and Abu Bakr, meaning "the glass is kindled." "Yūqadu" with lightening is read by the Syrians, Nafi' and Hafs, and "tawaqqadu" (with the doubled letter) is read by the Makkans and the Basrans, meaning "this lamp is kindled." ﴿From a tree﴾, that is, the beginning of its kindling is from the oil of the olive tree, meaning that its wick is fed with its oil. ﴿Blessed﴾, abundant in benefits. Or, because it grew in the land which was blessed for the worlds. It was said: seventy prophets, among them Ibrahim, peace be upon him, invoked blessings upon it. ﴿Olive﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "tree," and it is its description (na't). ﴿Neither eastern nor western﴾, that is, its place of growth is Syria, meaning it is neither from the east nor from the west, but in the middle between them, and that is Syria; and the finest olive oil is the oil of Syria. It was also said: it is not one that the sun shines upon only at the time of its rising or its setting, but it receives it both in the morning and in the evening, so it is both eastern and western. ﴿Its oil almost gives light﴾, its oil (duhn), ﴿though no fire touches it﴾. The oil is described as pure and shining, and that because of its sheen it almost gives light without fire.

(p-507) ﴿Light upon light﴾, that is, this light by which the Real is likened is a doubled light, in which the niche, the glass, the lamp and the oil have united in support, so that nothing remains of what could strengthen the light. This is because a lamp, when it is in a confined place like a niche, is more gathered in its light, unlike a wide place, where the light spreads out. The lantern is the most helpful thing for increasing illumination, and likewise the oil and its purity. The striking of a parable is done with something base, perceptible and familiar, not with something lofty, unseen and unwitnessed. Thus, when Abu Tammam said about al-Ma'mun:

"The valour of Amr in the generosity of Hatim, in the forbearance of al-Ahnaf, in the intelligence of Iyas."

It was said to him: "The Caliph is above those whom you have compared him to." Whereupon he improvised:

"Do not deny my striking a parable with one who falls short of him in generosity and valour."

"So Allah has struck the lesser for His light, a parable of the niche and the lamp."

﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills﴾, that is, to this piercing light, ﴿whom He wills﴾ of His servants, that is, He grants success in reaching the truth to whom He wills of His servants, by inspiration from Allah or by their reflection upon the proof. ﴿And Allah strikes parables for mankind﴾, bringing them near to their understandings, so that they may take heed and believe. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, so He makes every thing clear by that by which it can be known.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The likeness of His light", that is, the light of Allah with which He guided the believer. Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah have mercy on him, recited, "The likeness of His light in the heart of the believer is like a niche," and Ubayy recited, "The likeness of the light of the believer."

In houses (﴿فِي بُيُوتٍ﴾) is related to "a niche," meaning: like a niche in some of the houses of Allah, which are the mosques. It is as if it were said: "The likeness of His light is as you see in the mosque, the light of the niche, whose description is such and such." Or it is related to "is kindled," meaning it is kindled in houses. Or it is related to "glorify," meaning men glorify Him in houses. "Therein" (فِيها) is a repetition for emphasis, like "Zayd is in the house, sitting therein." Or it is related to something omitted, meaning: they glorified [Him] in houses.

﴿Allah has ordained﴾, i.e., commanded, ﴿that it be raised﴾, i.e., built, ﴿and that His name be remembered therein﴾ [Q. 2:127: "And when Abraham was raising the foundations"]. Or it means "be exalted," from elevation (al-ri'fah). From al-Hasan: Allah did not command that it be raised by construction, but by glorifying it.

﴿and that His name be remembered therein﴾ means that His Book is recited therein. Or it is general for every kind of remembrance.

﴿He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings﴾, i.e., He is prayed to therein at dawn, meaning the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-fajr), and in the evenings, meaning the noon and afternoon prayers and the two night prayers (the evening and the night prayers). He used the singular for "mornings" because the morning prayer is one prayer, whereas there are several prayers in the evenings. Al-āṣāl (الآصال) is the plural of uṣul (أُصُل), which is the plural of aṣīl (أصِيل), meaning the late afternoon and evening (al-ʿashiyy).

(p-508)

﴿Men﴾ is the subject (fā'il) of "yusabbihu" (glorifies). "Yusabbaḥu" (is glorified) is read by Shāmī (Ibn ʿĀmir, the Syrian reader) and Abū Bakr (ʿAsim's transmitter). It is then attributed to one of the three adverbial phrases, namely ﴿for Him therein in the mornings﴾ [al-Nūr: 36]. ﴿Men﴾ is in the nominative case, governed by what is indicated by "yusabbihu," meaning: they glorify Him. ﴿Neither trade﴾ means they are not distracted by it, ﴿nor sale﴾ means they are not distracted from it. ﴿Trade﴾ refers to commerce while travelling, and ﴿sale﴾ to commerce at home. It has been said that "trade" means buying, using the generic noun (ism al-jins, a noun referring to a whole category) to refer to one of its types. Or "sale" is singled out after the general term, because it is more absorbing in distraction than buying, since the profit in a profitable sale is certain, whereas in buying it is only presumed. ﴿From the remembrance of God﴾ means with the tongue and the heart. ﴿And the establishment of prayer﴾ means from establishing the prayer. The tāʾ in "iqāmah" (establishment) is a substitute (ʿiwaḍ, something put in place of a dropped element) for the dropped ʿayn, due to morphological alteration (iʿlāl, the changing of weak letters). The original form was "iqwām." When the waw became an alif, two alifs came together, so one was deleted because of the meeting of two unvocalised letters, and the tāʾ was added as a substitute for the deleted letter. When it was made a construct (idāfah), the construct replaced the tāʾ and so it was dropped. ﴿And the giving of zakat﴾ means and from giving zakat. The meaning is: they have no trade that would distract them, like those who seclude themselves in isolation, or they buy and sell and remember God while doing so. When the prayer time comes, they rise to it without reluctance, like those who live among people. ﴿They fear a Day﴾ means the Day of Resurrection. "They fear" is either a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the pronoun in "tulhīhim," or another description of ﴿men﴾. ﴿On which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾: the hearts, by reaching the throats, and the eyes, by staring and fixing in terror. Or it means: the hearts turn toward faith after disbelief, and the eyes turn toward seeing after denying the rebellion, as in His saying: ﴿So We removed from you your covering, and today your sight is sharp﴾ [Qāf: 22].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 38:

﴿That Allah may reward them with the best of what they did, and increase them from His bounty.﴾ Meaning: they glorify (Him) and fear (Him). (p-509) ﴿That Allah may reward them with the best﴾ — the reward for their deeds; that is, that He may give them their reward multiplied, and increase them beyond the reward promised for the deed, out of His grace. ﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning.﴾ That is, He rewards whom He wills with a reward that does not enter into the reckoning of creatures. These are the attributes of those who are guided by the light of Allah. As for those who have strayed from it, they are those mentioned in His saying.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 39:

﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage﴾ — it is what is seen in the desert, from the light of the sun at midday, shimmering over the surface of the earth, appearing as if it were flowing water. ﴿In a valley﴾ — a qa' (valley floor), or the plural of qa', which is the level, flat land, like the jirah (pebble) in jar (a stream bed). ﴿The thirsty one thinks it to be water﴾ — the thirsty one supposes it to be water. ﴿Until, when he comes to it﴾ — that is, he comes to what he imagined to be water. ﴿He finds it to be nothing﴾ — as he supposed. ﴿And he finds Allah﴾ — that is, the recompense of Allah, as in His saying ﴿He will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [an-Nisa: 110], meaning he will find His forgiveness and mercy. ﴿With Him﴾ — with the disbeliever. ﴿So He pays him his account in full﴾ — that is, He gives him the full and complete recompense for his deeds. He used the singular after the plural, taking each one of the disbelievers as the referent. ﴿And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ — because He does not need to count or calculate, and no reckoning preoccupies Him from another reckoning, or His reckoning is near, because what is coming is near. He likened the deeds of one who does not believe in faith and does not follow the truth, which he thinks will benefit him with Allah and save him from His punishment, and then in the end his hope is disappointed and he meets the opposite of what he decreed, to a mirage that the disbeliever sees in the desert (al-sahirah), when thirst of the Day of Resurrection has overcome him. So he supposes it to be water and goes to it, but finds nothing of what he hoped for, and finds the angels of Allah (zabaniyah) with him, who seize him and drag him toward Hell, and they give him to drink of boiling water and purulent discharge (ghassaq). These are the ones of whom Allah said: ﴿Labouring, weary﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 3], and ﴿while they think they are doing good works﴾ [al-Kahf: 104]. It was said that it was revealed concerning Utbah ibn Rabi'ah ibn Umayyah, who used to practise asceticism seeking religion in the Jahiliyyah, but when Islam came, he disbelieved.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 40:

﴿Or like darknesses in a deep sea﴾ Here "aw" (or) is like the "aw" in the sense of "or" as in the previous comparison. ﴿Deep﴾ (lujjiyy): profound, with much water; it is a relative adjective derived from al-lujj, which is the greater part of the sea's water. (p-510) ﴿Covers it﴾ (yaghshahu): covers the sea, or whoever is in it; that is, it rises over it and covers it. ﴿A wave﴾ (mawj): this is what rises of the water. ﴿Above it a wave﴾: that is, above the wave there is another wave. ﴿Above it clouds﴾: above the highest wave there are clouds. ﴿Darknesses﴾: that is, these are darknesses: the darkness of the clouds, the darkness of the wave, and the darkness of the sea. ﴿One above another﴾: the darkness of the wave upon the darkness of the sea, the darkness of the wave upon the wave, and the darkness of the clouds upon the wave. ﴿If he brings out his hand﴾: that is, the one who is in it. ﴿He can hardly see it﴾: an intensification of "he did not see it," meaning he is hardly close to seeing it, let alone actually seeing it. He first likened their deeds to a mirage, whose benefit is lost and whose harm is present, which a traveler from afar takes for water, finds nothing, and whose disappointment and grief are not lessened by finding, as with others of the mirage, something; until he finds the guards (al-zabaniyah) dragging him to the Fire. Second, he likened them, in their darkness and blackness, because they are void, and in their emptiness of the light of truth, to layered darknesses from the depth of the sea, the waves, and the clouds. ﴿And whomever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾: whomever Allah does not guide, will not be guided. From al-Zajjaj. In a hadith: "Allah created the creation in darkness, then sprinkled upon them of His light; whoever is struck by that light is guided, and whoever misses it goes astray."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 41:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ — Have you not known, O Muhammad, with a knowledge that stands in place of direct seeing in certainty — ﴿that to Allah glorifies whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds, spreading their wings⦆ — ﴿that Allah glorifies whoever is in the heavens and the earth and the birds in flight﴾. The phrase ﴿whoever﴾ is conjoined (ʿatf) to "man" (the preceding word in the verse). ﴿Spreading their wings﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the birds, meaning: they arrange their wings in the air. ﴿Each one has known its prayer and its glorification﴾ — the pronoun in ʿalima (has known) refers either to each one (kull) or to Allah, and likewise the pronoun in "its prayer" and "its glorification." Ṣalāh (prayer) here means supplication (duʿāʾ). It is not far-fetched that Allah inspires the birds with His supplication and glorification, just as He inspires them with the many subtle sciences that intelligent beings barely manage to arrive at. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾ — nothing escapes His knowledge.

To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth (﴿وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾), because He is their Creator, and whoever owns anything does so by His giving him ownership of it. ﴿And to Allah is the final return﴾ (﴿وَإلى اللهِ المَصِيرُ﴾), the return of all things.

Have you not seen that Allah drives (ﷻ) [the clouds]: He leads them wherever He wills. ﴿Clouds﴾ is the plural of *sahabah* (a single cloud), as shown by ﴿then He gathers them together﴾, where the verb is masculine because the word is treated as a collective noun, meaning He joins one part of it to another. ﴿Then He makes it into heaped-up masses﴾, piled one upon another. ﴿Then you see the rain﴾, the rainwater, ﴿coming out from within it﴾, from its openings and outlets. *Khilal* is the plural of *khalal* (gap), like *jibal* (mountains) for *jabal* (mountain). ﴿And He sends down﴾: the reading *wa-yunzilu* is attributed to the readers of Makka, Madina and Basra. ﴿from the sky﴾: *min* here marks the starting point (*li-ibtida' al-ghaya*, "the starting point of the limit"), because the beginning of the descent is from the sky. ﴿mountains﴾ *min jibal*: *min* here is partitive (*lil-tab'id*, "indicating a part"), because what Allah sends down is only part of those mountains which are ﴿in it﴾, in the sky, ﴿of hail﴾: *min* here is explanatory (*lil-bayan*, "explaining what is meant"), or the first *min* is for the starting point and the second for the partitive. The meaning is: He sends down hail from the sky, from mountains within it. According to the first view, the object of *yunazzilu* is *min jibal*, meaning some mountains within it. The meaning of ﴿mountains in it of hail﴾ is that Allah creates mountains of hail in the sky, just as He created mountains of stone on the earth; or the mention of mountains is meant to indicate abundance, as one says, "So-and-so owns mountains of gold." ﴿So He strikes with it﴾, with the hail, ﴿whom He wills﴾, that is, He strikes people and their crops. ﴿And He averts it from whom He wills﴾, so that it does not strike them; or He punishes whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills, so that He does not punish them. ﴿The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight﴾, its light nearly snatches the eyes away. The reading *yudhhibu* (causing to go) means *yazidu* (it increases), with the extra *ba'* (as in *yadhhabu bi-*, "takes away with").

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 44:

﴿Allah turns the night and the day around﴾ He causes them to alternate, varying in length and shortness, and in succession. ﴿Indeed, in that is a lesson﴾ in the driving of the clouds, the sending down of rain and hail, and the turning of night and day. ﴿A lesson for those endowed with insight﴾, that is, for those possessing intellects. This is from the enumeration of the proofs of His lordship, since He mentioned the glorification of all who are in the heavens and the earth and what flies between them, their supplication to Him, and the subjection of the clouds, and so on to the end of what He mentioned. These are manifest demonstrations of His existence and clear indications of His attributes for whoever looks and reflects. Then He presented another proof, so He said, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 24, verse 45:

﴿And Allah created every﴾ "*khāliqu kulli*" (creator of every): read by Ḥamzah and ʿAlī. ﴿creature (*dābbah*)﴾: every animal (*ḥayawān*) that crawls (*yadibbu*) upon the face of the earth. ﴿from water﴾: that is, from a kind of water specific to that creature, or from a particular water, which is the *nutfah* (drop of seminal fluid). Then He made the created beings differ from the *nutfah*: some of them are creeping things (*hawāmm*), some are cattle (*bahāʾim*), and some are human beings (*anāsī*). This is like His saying: ﴿Watered with one water, yet We make some of them excel others in food﴾ [al-Raʿd: 4]. This is evidence that they have a Creator and Governor; otherwise they would not differ, since their origin is one. He used the definite form "the water" in His saying ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 30] because the intended meaning there is that the kinds of living creatures are created from the kind of water, and that it is the origin, even if intermediate means come between it and them. They said: the first thing Allah created was water, and from it He created fire, wind, and clay. From fire He created the jinn, from wind the angels, and from clay Adam and the beasts of the earth. Since the word "creature" (*dābbah*) includes both the discerning and the non-discerning, the discerning ones were given precedence, and what is beyond them was given their rule, as if all creatures were discerning. For this reason it is said: ﴿Some of them walk on their bellies﴾, like the serpent and the fish. Crawling on the belly was called "walking" by way of *istiʿārah* (metaphor), as one says of a continuing matter, "this matter has walked on," or by way of *mushākalah* (contextual correspondence), because the crawler is mentioned alongside the walkers. ﴿And some of them walk on two legs﴾, like humans and birds. ﴿And some of them walk on four﴾, like cattle. He began with what is most evident as a display of power, namely that which walks without any instrument of walking, whether legs or otherwise, then that which walks on two legs, then that which walks on four. ﴿Allah creates what He wills﴾ however He wills. ﴿Indeed Allah is over all things Competent﴾: nothing is beyond His ability.

Quran 24:46 with the commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil):

﴿Indeed We have sent down verses that make things clear, and Allah guides whom He wills﴾ by His kindness and His will ﴿to a straight path﴾, to the religion of Islam, which leads to His Paradise. So the verses are for establishing His proof.

When He mentioned the sending down of the verses, He mentioned after them the division of people into three groups: a group that affirmed outwardly and denied inwardly, and they are the hypocrites (munafiqun); a group that affirmed both outwardly and inwardly, and they are the sincere (mukhlisun); and a group that denied both outwardly and inwardly, and they are the disbelievers (kafirun).
